title: Objection delivery and required hearing
mainQuestion: How does a person object to confirmation of a surveyed boundary, and what hearing follows a timely objection?
studySummary: A person objecting to boundary confirmation must deliver a written objection statement to the Registrar General by an approved delivery method before the notice deadline. If that statement is delivered on time in accordance with subsection 10(1), the Registrar General shall hold a hearing on the validity of the objection and, where applicable, the applicant's claim about the boundaries shown on the plan of survey.

objectives.objective: Recall how an objection to boundary confirmation must be delivered.
objectives.guidedQuestion: How must a person deliver an objection to confirmation of a boundary shown on a plan of survey?
objectives.studyAnswer: The person shall deliver to the Registrar General, by personal service, registered mail, or courier service before the deadline stipulated in the notice under subsection 9(1) or (2), a written statement setting out the reasons for and any grounds and arguments for the objection.

evidence.evidenceText: A person who wishes to object to the confirmation of a boundary as shown on the plan of survey shall deliver to the Registrar General by personal service, registered mail or courier service before the deadline stipulated in the notice sent under subsection 9(1) or (2), a written statement setting out the reasons for and any grounds and arguments in relation to the objection.

objectives.objective: Recall the hearing required after a timely objection statement.
objectives.guidedQuestion: What hearing must the Registrar General hold after a timely written objection is delivered?
objectives.studyAnswer: If the written statement of objection is delivered before the deadline in accordance with subsection 10(1), the Registrar General shall hold a hearing to determine the validity of the objection and, if applicable, the validity of the applicant's claim that the boundaries lie as shown on the plan of survey.

evidence.evidenceText: If a written statement of objection is delivered before the deadline in accordance with subsection (1), the Registrar General shall hold a hearing to determine the validity of the objection and, if applicable, the validity of the applicant’s claim that the boundaries lie as shown on the plan of survey.

title: No-objection confirmation or hearing decision
mainQuestion: What may the Registrar General do when no timely written objection is delivered in a boundary-confirmation proceeding?
studySummary: When no written objection is delivered before the subsection 10(1) deadline, the Registrar General has two possible paths based on the material filed. If satisfied that the boundaries should be confirmed, the Registrar General may confirm them as shown on the plan of survey without a hearing; if not satisfied, the Registrar General may hold a hearing under the Act and regulations.

objectives.guidedQuestion: What condition activates the Registrar General's subsection 10(3) choices?
objectives.studyAnswer: Subsection 10(3) applies if no written statement of objection is delivered before the deadline in accordance with subsection 10(1).

title: Hearing parties and notice contents
mainQuestion: Who participates in a boundary-confirmation hearing, and what notice must the Registrar General cause to be given?
studySummary: For a hearing under section 10, the parties include the applicant, objectors who delivered a statement under subsection 10(1), and any other persons specified by the Registrar General. The Registrar General shall cause notice of hearing to be given to the parties and specified others, and the notice must state hearing logistics, describe the application or proceeding reasons, set out grounds and arguments, describe objections received, and otherwise comply with the regulations.

objectives.objective: Recall who are parties to a section 10 hearing.
objectives.guidedQuestion: Who are parties to a boundary-confirmation hearing held under section 10?
objectives.studyAnswer: The parties are any applicant, any person who delivers a statement of objection under subsection 10(1), and such other persons as the Registrar General specifies.

evidence.evidenceText: Any applicant, any person who delivers a statement of objection under subsection (1) and such other persons as the Registrar General specifies are parties to a hearing held under this section.

objectives.objective: Recall who must receive notice of hearing.
objectives.guidedQuestion: To whom must the Registrar General cause notice of hearing to be given?
objectives.studyAnswer: The Registrar General shall cause notice of hearing to be given, in accordance with subsection 10(6), to the parties and to such other persons as the Registrar General specifies.

evidence.evidenceText: The Registrar General shall cause a notice of hearing to be given, in accordance with subsection (6), to the parties and to such other persons as the Registrar General specifies.

objectives.objective: Recall the required contents and form of a hearing notice.
objectives.guidedQuestion: What must a section 10 hearing notice specify or contain?
objectives.studyAnswer: The notice shall specify the date, time, and place of the hearing; contain a description of the reasons for the application or proceeding; set out grounds and arguments in relation to it; describe the reasons and grounds and arguments in any objections received; and otherwise be given in accordance with the regulations.

evidence.evidenceText: A notice given under subsection (5) shall specify the date, time and place of the hearing, shall contain a description of the reasons for the making of the application or the initiating of the proceeding, as the case may be, shall set out any grounds and arguments in relation to it, shall describe the reasons and set out the grounds and arguments contained in any objections received and shall otherwise be given in accordance with the regulations.

title: Corrected boundary-confirmation plan of survey
mainQuestion: How may a filed boundary-confirmation plan of survey be corrected, and what happens after the corrected plan is filed?
studySummary: On satisfactory evidence, the Registrar General may order a corrected plan of survey to address an inconsistency, error, or omission in a plan filed under subsection 15(1), with notice given as considered appropriate or no notice. A correction cannot affect a confirmed and certified boundary. The corrected plan must be filed as required, subsection 15(2) applies with necessary modifications, and the superseded original plan must be noted accordingly.

objectives.objective: Recall when the Registrar General may order a corrected plan of survey.
objectives.guidedQuestion: When may the Registrar General order that a corrected plan of survey be made?
objectives.studyAnswer: Subject to subsection 16(3), the Registrar General may, on receiving satisfactory evidence, order a corrected plan of survey to correct an inconsistency, error, or omission in a plan of survey filed under subsection 15(1).

evidence.evidenceText: Subject to subsection (3), the Registrar General may, on receiving satisfactory evidence, order that a corrected plan of survey be made in order to correct any inconsistency, error or omission in a plan of survey that has been filed under subsection 15(1).

objectives.objective: Recall the Registrar General's notice discretion before a correction order.
objectives.guidedQuestion: What notice may the Registrar General give before making a corrected-plan order?
objectives.studyAnswer: Before making an order, the Registrar General may give such notice to interested parties as the Registrar General considers appropriate, or may make the order without giving notice.

evidence.evidenceText: The Registrar General may give such notice to interested parties as the Registrar General considers appropriate before making an order under subsection (1) or may make the order without giving notice.

objectives.objective: Recall the boundary-location limit on corrections.
objectives.guidedQuestion: What effect may a correction under section 16 have on a confirmed and certified boundary?
objectives.studyAnswer: A correction under section 16 shall not affect the location of a boundary that has been confirmed and certified under the Act.

evidence.evidenceText: A correction under this section shall not affect the location of a boundary that has been confirmed and certified under this Act.

objectives.objective: Recall the filing and notation steps for a corrected plan.
objectives.guidedQuestion: What must happen when a corrected plan of survey is made and filed?
objectives.studyAnswer: The Registrar General shall cause the corrected plan to be filed in accordance with the regulations and with the Registry Act or Land Titles Act, subsection 15(2) applies with necessary modifications, and when it is filed the Registrar General shall cause a notation on the related subsection 15(1) plan stating that it is superseded by the corrected plan.

evidence.evidenceText: The Registrar General shall cause a corrected plan of survey made under subsection (1) to be filed in accordance with the regulations and with the Registry Act or the Land Titles Act, as the case may be.
Subsection 15(2) applies with the necessary modifications to a corrected plan of survey filed under subsection (4).

When a corrected plan of survey is filed under subsection (4), the Registrar General shall cause a notation to be made on the plan of survey filed under subsection 15(1) to which the corrected plan relates, to the effect that it is superseded by the corrected plan.

title: Coordinate monument and coordinate survey system definitions
mainQuestion: What do coordinate monument and coordinate survey system mean in the Surveys Act?
studySummary: The Surveys Act defines a coordinate monument by its physical form and by its establishment and maintenance under section 3. It defines the coordinate survey system by reference to the system established under section 2.

objectives.objective: Recall the definition of coordinate monument.
objectives.guidedQuestion: What is a coordinate monument under the Surveys Act?
objectives.studyAnswer: A coordinate monument is a brass, bronze, or aluminum cap or plate established and maintained in accordance with section 3.

objectives.guidedQuestion: What is a coordinate survey system under the Surveys Act?
objectives.studyAnswer: A coordinate survey system is a system established under section 2.

title: Corner and legal monument definitions
mainQuestion: How does the Surveys Act define a corner and a legal monument?
studySummary: The selected definitions distinguish a boundary point from a survey device. A corner is a point in an intersection of land boundaries, while a legal monument is a device planted by a surveyor.

title: Director of Surveys designation and coordinate monument duties
mainQuestion: How are Director of Surveys roles designated, and what coordinate monument duty does the Director have?
studySummary: Service New Brunswick shall designate a surveyor as Director of Surveys. It may also designate one or more eligible surveyors to perform specified duties or exercise specified powers of the Director. For the coordinate survey system, the Director shall establish and maintain suitably inscribed coordinate monuments made of brass, bronze, or aluminum and placed in one of the stated ways.

objectives.objective: Recall who designates the Director of Surveys.
objectives.guidedQuestion: Who must designate the Director of Surveys, and who must be designated?
objectives.studyAnswer: Service New Brunswick shall designate a surveyor as Director of Surveys.

evidence.evidenceText: Service New Brunswick shall designate a surveyor as Director of Surveys.

objectives.objective: Recall the power to designate surveyors for Director duties or powers.
objectives.guidedQuestion: What may Service New Brunswick authorize designated surveyors to do for the Director of Surveys?
objectives.studyAnswer: Service New Brunswick may designate one or more surveyors to perform any of the Director of Surveys' duties or exercise any of the Director's powers that are specified in the designation.

evidence.evidenceText: Service New Brunswick may designate one or more surveyors to perform any of the duties or exercise any of the powers of the Director of Surveys that are specified in the designation.

objectives.objective: Recall eligibility for a designation under subsection 3(1.1).
objectives.guidedQuestion: Who is eligible to be designated under subsection 3(1.1)?
objectives.studyAnswer: Only a surveyor who is an employee of Service New Brunswick or an employee under the Civil Service Act is eligible to be designated under subsection 3(1.1).

evidence.evidenceText: Only a surveyor who is an employee of Service New Brunswick or an employee under the Civil Service Act is eligible to be designated under subsection (1.1).
